questions.question: Foundation Define the term compound and give one example.

points.text: A compound is a substance made from two or more elements that are chemically combined in fixed proportions. Example: water (H₂O) is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen.

questions.question: Foundation Explain the difference between a mixture and a compound.

points.text: A compound has elements chemically combined in fixed proportions and can only be separated by chemical reactions. A mixture has substances not chemically combined, with variable proportions, and can be separated by physical methods (filtration, distillation, etc.).

questions.question: Foundation Balance the following equation: H₂ + O₂ → H₂O

points.text: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. Count: Left = H: 4, O: 2; Right = H: 4, O: 2. Balanced.

questions.question: Higher Write a balanced symbol equation with state symbols for the reaction of calcium with oxygen to form calcium oxide, CaO.

points.text: 2Ca(s) + O₂(g) → 2CaO(s). Calcium is a solid metal, oxygen is a gas, and calcium oxide is a solid.

questions.question: Higher Balance the following equation: Al + O₂ → Al₂O₃

points.text: 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃. Check: Left = Al: 4, O: 6; Right = Al: 4, O: 6. Balanced.

questions.question: Foundation Give the chemical symbols for: sodium, potassium, iron, chlorine, calcium.

points.text: Sodium = Na, Potassium = K, Iron = Fe, Chlorine = Cl, Calcium = Ca. (Na and K come from their Latin names: natrium and kalium.)

markScheme.exemplarAnswer: An element is a substance made of only one type of atom and cannot be broken down chemically (e.g. Fe, O₂). A compound is a substance made from two or more elements chemically combined in fixed proportions; it can only be separated into elements by chemical reactions (e.g. H₂O always has 2 H : 1 O). A mixture contains two or more substances not chemically combined, so the substances retain their individual properties and proportions can vary; mixtures can be separated by physical methods such as filtration, distillation or chromatography. Mark scheme: 1 mark for each correct definition (element, compound, mixture — up to 3); 1 mark for stating compounds have fixed proportions; 1 mark for stating mixtures have variable proportions; 1 mark for correct separation methods for each; 1 mark for using examples.
